evidence.text: Does uplifting a nonperturbatively stabilized type-IIB AdS vacuum leave a sufficiently broad barrier against volume decompactification?

evidence.text: Which constrained integer-flux configurations yield stable non-supersymmetric dS or AdS extrema in an isotropic type IIB non-geometric model, and do the reported dS examples admit small-field, multi-field slow-roll conditions?

sources.title: More stable de Sitter vacua from S-dual nongeometric fluxes

evidence.text: Can S-dual nongeometric P-fluxes and torus anisotropy produce further stable dS/AdS candidates, remove instabilities hidden by isotropic truncations, and change the moduli hierarchies relevant to small-field inflation?

sources.title: Stability, Tunneling and Flux Changing de Sitter Transitions in the Large Volume String Scenario

evidence.text: Are non-supersymmetric LVS AdS minima nonperturbatively stable within effective field theory, and how do uplifted dS vacua decay through flux-changing brane nucleation and tunneling to decompactification?

sources.title: Heterotic Moduli Stabilisation and Non-Supersymmetric Vacua

evidence.text: Can heterotic geometric moduli and the dilaton be stabilized perturbatively in finite-coupling, nonsupersymmetric vacua, and can the resulting AdS minima be lifted to dS?

sources.title: Revisiting constraints on uplifts to de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Can brane-based uplifts of type IIB AdS vacua satisfy both the integrated Gibbons–Maldacena–Nuñez constraint and the constraint reproducing four-dimensional Einstein equations, rather than only giving a positive four-dimensional effective potential?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Can positive energy uplift a quantum-stabilized AdS vacuum while preserving stabilization? The relevant starting data include supersymmetry, nonzero superpotential, and whether stabilization uses KKLT, LVS, or more elaborate nonperturbative effects.

sources.title: Crisis on Infinite Earths: Short-lived de Sitter Vacua in the String Theory Landscape

evidence.text: Can additional AdS decay destinations make uplifted string-theoretic dS vacua short-lived enough to satisfy the assumed TCC bound, and are the underlying static four-dimensional assumptions compatible with higher-dimensional equations?

sources.title: The gravitino and the swampland

evidence.text: Can an AdS tower argument survive an uplift to positive vacuum energy? The proposed transfer assumes that a positive inverse-volume contribution shifts the stabilized moduli only slightly.

sources.title: Metastable vacua from torsion and machine learning

evidence.text: Can torsional five-form contributions and wrapped non-BPS branes provide minimal ingredients for classically stable non-SUSY AdS vacua and their uplift to dS, and what possible instabilities remain?

sources.title: Non-supersymmetric AdS from string theory

evidence.text: Can the non-supersymmetric heterotic string support parametrically controlled AdS3 backgrounds without perturbative scalar instabilities, including vacua supported essentially by string loops? Can its positive one-loop vacuum energy instead produce de Sitter space?

sources.title: The Uplifton

evidence.text: Can a neutral, smooth, horizonless massive object preserve four-dimensional Lorentz invariance and serve as an AdS-to-de Sitter uplift ingredient while avoiding some charged-antibrane complications?

sources.title: O(16) × O(16) heterotic theory on AdS$_{3}$× S$^{3}$× T$^{4}$

evidence.text: Can the one-loop potential uplift non-supersymmetric O(16) × O(16) heterotic AdS3 × S3 × T4 vacua to de Sitter, and which gravitational and torus-modulus fluctuations remain perturbatively stable?

sources.title: (A)dS backgrounds from asymmetric orientifolds

evidence.text: Can asymmetric orientifold projections and discrete RR fluxes remove NSNS runaway directions and stabilize the dilaton at weak coupling, producing critical-string AdS6 backgrounds and a supercritical-string metastable dS4 candidate?

sources.title: Raising Anti de Sitter vacua to de Sitter vacua in heterotic M-theory

evidence.text: Can stabilized heterotic M-theory AdS vacua be raised to metastable dS vacua using anomalous-U(1) Fayet–Iliopoulos terms or nonsupersymmetric brane-tension corrections, while allowing a small cosmological constant?

sources.title: Lifetime of Stringy de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Preserve the axion isometry during stabilization, gauge it with magnetic D7 flux, and use the positive D-term for uplift. The isometry is an input condition, so the construction cannot be transferred unchanged to a shift-breaking superpotential.

sources.title: Slow-Roll Inflation in Non-geometric Flux Compactification

evidence.text: Integer flux configurations satisfying R-R tadpole, T-dual tadpole and Q·H3=Q·Q=0 Bianchi constraints are generated before numerical minimisation. A genetic algorithm searches the six real moduli with stated convergence criterion 10^-20 and a finite flux cutoff.

sources.title: More stable de Sitter vacua from S-dual nongeometric fluxes

evidence.text: The displayed superpotential is W=P₀−SP₁+Σm(P₂m−SP₃m)Um, with cubic polynomials in the complex-structure fields and coefficients determined by fluxes. The Kähler potential is K=−Σi=1⁷ln(2ψi). Numerical mass matrices, F-terms and gravitino quantities characterize the candidates.

sources.title: Stability, Tunneling and Flux Changing de Sitter Transitions in the Large Volume String Scenario

evidence.text: Use Brown–Teitelboim Euclidean brane nucleation for transitions between flux sectors, which correspond to different effective potentials. Use Coleman–De Luccia tunneling for decompactification at fixed flux within one effective potential.

sources.title: Heterotic Moduli Stabilisation and Non-Supersymmetric Vacua

evidence.text: Uses algebraic stationary-point analysis with STRINGVACUA for a simple example and numerical continuation from aligned D-terms to deformed configurations. Uplift searches examine the effective dilaton potential, loop corrections and nonperturbative superpotential terms.

sources.title: Revisiting constraints on uplifts to de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Represents nonperturbative, α′ and string-loop effects as potential shifts in the two traced constraints. Primed and unprimed corrections are distinguished because their contributions depend on their ten-dimensional origin and need not coincide.

sources.title: Four-dimensional de Sitter cosmology on D-branes nucleated in an asymptotically $\text{AdS}_5\times T^{1,1}$ background

evidence.text: Can order-α′² corrections produce a small positive four-dimensional vacuum energy on D3-branes or wrapped D5-branes nucleating from a charged asymptotically AdS5×T1,1 background, while satisfying the phenomenological constraints adopted in the paper?

sources.title: Metastable vacua from torsion and machine learning

evidence.text: Can the proposed classical AdS and uplifted dS candidates remain compatible with conjectured quantum-gravity restrictions on non-supersymmetric vacua, scale separation and positive scalar-potential minima?

sources.title: Supersymmetry Breaking Warped Throats and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a throat with slowly running AdS-like asymptotics contain a stable supersymmetry-breaking infrared sector? The motivating application is redshifted vacuum energy for four-dimensional uplift.

sources.title: An attempt to derive the LVS from a 10d EFT perspective

evidence.text: Can the pre-uplift LVS AdS potential, including its leading volume suppressions, be recovered directly from ten-dimensional EFT without assuming four-dimensional supergravity? The paper investigates a conditional mismatch rather than establishing failure of LVS.

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: How do potential values and other features vary across the critical points found by ANN+GA? The analyzed sample includes AdS and dS points without imposing stability, and distinguishes two flux cases.

sources.title: Towards a naturally small cosmological constant from branes in 6-D supergravity

evidence.text: Can classical self-tuning in six-dimensional supergravity cancel large brane vacuum energies and remain sufficiently stable under quantum corrections to leave a four-dimensional energy density of order 1/r^4?

evidence.text: Do branes sourcing AdS flux vacua decouple from the asymptotic bulk at low energy, including proposed scale-separated vacua with unusual asymptotic geometry? The diagnostic is propagation of minimally coupled scalar waves between the throat and large radial distance.

sources.title: Backtracking AdS flux vacua

evidence.text: Use supersymmetric-domain-wall or fake-superpotential techniques to replace second-order equations by first-order flows generated by P. Dimensional reduction supplies the universal-modulus dependence of curvature, NS flux and RR flux terms.

sources.title: On the DGKT brane dual and its decoupling

evidence.text: Flux backtracking solves BPS flow equations using fluxes that do not scale with N. A harmonic superposition ansatz then introduces the D4 stacks. The author reports checking the ten-dimensional Einstein and dilaton equations and imposing D4 flux quantization.

sources.title: On the branes behind scale-separated AdS$_{3}$ flux vacua

evidence.text: Flux backtracking switches off f7 and f31,f32,f33, solves flat-sliced three-dimensional domain-wall BPS equations obtained by completing squares, and uplifts using explicit metric and dilaton formulae.

sources.title: Low-energy brane decoupling in AdS flux vacua

evidence.text: Flux backtracking identifies asymptotic moduli trajectories and potential steepness. The asymptotic radial wave equation defines an effective transverse dimension and phase-space factor. Formal sphere reduction is used to identify generalized Freund–Rubin potentials.

sources.title: Backtracking AdS flux vacua

evidence.text: Calibration examples recover the known Freund–Rubin cones, flat-space D3/M2/M5 pictures, and the ABJM orbifold after an eleven-dimensional uplift. These are reported checks against known brane descriptions.

sources.title: Backtracking AdS flux vacua

evidence.text: Remove selected brane-sourced fluxes from the off-shell scalar potential, solve a horizonless radial running solution, and uplift it. The radial ansatz is ds_d²=dr²+e^(2A(r))ds_flat,d−1² with scalar profiles depending only on r.

sources.title: Deforming AdS3×S3×T4AdS3×S3×T4 in Type IIB Supergravity

sources.title: AdS$_{D}$× I solutions in axio-dilaton gravity

sources.title: AdS in warped space-times

evidence.text: How can semi-localised brane intersections generate AdS factors whose warp factors depend only on internal coordinates, providing candidate AdS/CFT backgrounds and lower-dimensional gauged-supergravity embeddings?

sources.title: Note on a Paper by Ooguri and Vafa

evidence.text: How should the proposed exclusion of stable non-supersymmetric large-radius AdS be formulated using branes in noncompact space, and do non-supersymmetric CFT counterexamples yield supersymmetry-breaking Minkowski limits?

evidence.text: Does a restriction on non-BPS charged objects in flat space also exclude supersymmetry breaking imposed only at an AdS boundary? The paper separates these claims because the boundary condition is absent before the near-horizon limit.

evidence.text: Compare tension-mediated NSNS and charge-mediated RR exchange in common units. Force signs diagnose long-distance motion; separate tachyon or duality information supplies short-distance and nonperturbative channels.

sources.title: The Octagon at large M

evidence.text: A proposed dimer partial resolution is tested by checking whether the adjacent gauge factors can have equal ranks. Fractional-brane and orientifold rank shifts obstruct the face fusion used to realize the dangerous resolutions.

sources.title: AdS and dS entropy from string junctions: or, The Function of junction conjunctions

evidence.text: Uses the Susskind–Witten UV/IR cutoff argument, relating a CFT energy cutoff to an AdS area bound and the largest enclosed black hole. A heuristic comparison then moves Coulomb-branch branes behind a black-hole horizon.

sources.title: Non-supersymmetric AdS$_{6}$ and the swampland

evidence.text: Do non-supersymmetric AdS6 backgrounds associated with five-brane webs survive perturbative brane fluctuations and non-perturbative decay channels, permitting stable holographic five-dimensional CFTs?

sources.title: Backtracking AdS flux vacua

evidence.text: Can an AdS flux compactification be reverse-engineered into a singular geometry and brane probes whose near-horizon limit returns the vacuum, especially when its holographic CFT is unknown?

sources.title: Note on a Paper by Ooguri and Vafa

evidence.text: How should the proposed exclusion of stable non-supersymmetric large-radius AdS be formulated using branes in noncompact space, and do non-supersymmetric CFT counterexamples yield supersymmetry-breaking Minkowski limits?

sources.title: Non-supersymmetric AdS and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a non-supersymmetric AdS background supported by an electric higher-form flux define consistent Einstein holography? The relevant decay channel uses branes electrically charged under the AdS-supporting flux.

sources.title: Double-Trace Flows and the Swampland

evidence.text: Does a restriction on non-BPS charged objects in flat space also exclude supersymmetry breaking imposed only at an AdS boundary? The paper separates these claims because the boundary condition is absent before the near-horizon limit.

sources.title: Engineering a bosonic AdS / CFT correspondence

evidence.text: Can an added form flux support a tachyon-stable, non-supersymmetric bosonic AdS background and a conjectural boundary CFT, with finite-temperature scalar spectra interpreted as glueballs?

sources.title: Aspects of AdS flux vacua with integer conformal dimensions

evidence.text: What structures accompany integer conformal dimensions in DGKT-type flux vacua, and when can leading flux scalings be obtained from near-horizon geometries of intersecting D-brane domain walls?

sources.title: Non-supersymmetric AdS and the Swampland

evidence.text: Why do known non-supersymmetric higher-spin and SYK holographic examples not refute the proposed exclusion? Both retain towers of additional bulk degrees of freedom that obstruct the finite-field Einstein regime.

destination.question: How are topological field theories constructed, and how do their extended observables determine boundary structures and quantum equivalence?

sources.title: Chern-Simons theory with finite gauge group

evidence.text: Construct a mathematically explicit finite-gauge-group topological field theory from its classical action through path-integral quantization, retaining locality, automorphisms, boundary state spaces, and gluing.

sources.title: Coupling a QFT to a TQFT and Duality

evidence.text: Lattice dualizations use discrete Fourier transforms while retaining original variables and introducing gauge fields and Stueckelberg fields. This keeps global holonomies visible instead of solving flatness only locally.

sources.title: Topological Chern-Simons/Matter Theories

evidence.text: In product targets, calculate open-string states using Floer cochains and Dolbeault resolutions of Ext groups, then construct a Chern–Simons-type string-field action. A noncommutative deformation of the B-model changes the differential and produces nonzero Chern–Simons level.

sources.title: Higher central charges and topological boundaries in 2+1-dimensional TQFTs

evidence.text: Gauge nonanomalous one-form symmetry subgroups using sums over H²(M,L). Coprime finite first homology removes nontrivial backgrounds. Prime-power factorization of Abelian TQFTs and the Chinese remainder theorem isolate factors in the extended higher-charge test.

sources.title: Chern-Simons theory with finite gauge group

evidence.text: Quantize with the groupoid measure μ[P]=1/|Aut P|. The gluing proof tracks stabilizers and fibers of the bundle-gluing map, then combines the measure identity with classical line contraction.

sources.title: Coupling a QFT to a TQFT and Duality

evidence.text: Triangulated formulations use simplicial cochains, δ, cup products, and higher products ∪₁ and ∪₂. Their correction terms restore gauge invariance lost because the cochain cup product is not supercommutative.

sources.title: Coupling a QFT to a TQFT and Duality

evidence.text: Lagrange multipliers impose flatness or Bianchi identities; dualization produces equivalent BF, Higgs/Stueckelberg, and higher-form gauge descriptions. Global fields are described using patch data, Deligne–Beilinson cocycles, or differential characters rather than ordinary globally defined forms.

sources.title: Boundary Conditions and Unitarity: the Maxwell-Chern-Simons System in $AdS_3/CFT_2$

evidence.text: Which boundary conditions conserve the symplectic structure of Maxwell–Chern–Simons theory in asymptotically AdS3, and which survive bulk ghost and boundary unitarity tests, including conditions coupling massive modes to chiral currents?

sources.title: Higher Symmetry and Gapped Phases of Gauge Theories

evidence.text: Which TQFTs describe gapped gauge phases with simultaneous partial Higgsing and confinement, how are their actions and extended observables classified, and can they describe phases protected by higher symmetry?

sources.title: Topological boundary conditions in abelian Chern-Simons theory

evidence.text: Describe topological boundaries, boundary and boundary-changing lines, and surface defects in abelian Chern–Simons theory; partially construct their higher categorical structure and classify quantum theories using invertible duality walls.

sources.title: Reflection positivity and invertible topological phases

evidence.text: How should reflection positivity extend to fully extended invertible topological field theories, and how can their deformation classes inform the classification of invertible lattice phases from dimension and symmetry type?

sources.title: Classification of Abelian spin Chern-Simons theories

evidence.text: When do distinct classical U(1)ᴺ spin Chern–Simons actions define equivalent quantum theories, which invariants classify them, and what does that classification imply for fractional quantum Hall response?
